clue.text: Artist needing to make bed among exclusive American people

indicators.note: among says the artist's name sits within the word for exclusive

parts.note: exclusive rights are sole rights
Tracey Emin is the British artist famous for her installation My Bed

explanation.surface: A painter has to make a bed while living among a select group of Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing to make bed' is a playful pointer to Emin's best-known work, My Bed, rather than an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seminole are a Native American nation of Florida and Oklahoma.

clue.text: Bear witness to Robin's exploits and half show contempt

indicators.note: half asks for just the first portion of the expression for scorn

parts.note: to ...-... something is to dismiss it with contempt

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to testify about Robin Hood's deeds while being half scornful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear witness' looks like the verb 'testify'; it is a bear who witnessed Christopher Robin's adventures in the Winnie-the-Pooh stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnie-the-Pooh, A. A. Milne's bear, is the companion and witness of Christopher Robin's escapades.

clue.text: Magistrate and bachelor: I 9 10 22down 12

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
the linked entries read SPEAK WITH FORKED TONGUE, which means tell a falsehood

explanation.surface: A judge and an unmarried man declare themselves in the theme's words.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references build the theme phrase from the Lone Ranger films, a fancy way of saying 'tell a lie'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailie is a Scottish municipal officer who sits as a local magistrate.

clue.text: One of a number of popes taking pride in the family?

definitions.text: One of a number of popes
definitions.meaning: describes something relating to one of the many popes called Leo
lion-like, as lions live in family groups called prides

explanation.surface: A pontiff of a certain name is proud of his relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pride' is not self-esteem but a group of lions, so the second reading means lion-like.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both things pertaining to Pope Leo and things resembling a lion.

clue.text: Say nothing after exchange of sex tips — result of hot and steamy squeezing?

definitions.text: result of hot and steamy squeezing?

indicators.note: after puts the zero at the end
the tips of the word sex are its first and last letters, S and X, and one is exchanged for the other

parts.note: to express something is to say it
O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A risque story of swapping bedroom advice, ending in something hot and steamy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange of sex tips' swaps the X in EXPRESS for an S, giving ESPRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso coffee is made by forcing steam-hot water through tightly packed grounds.

clue.text: Media for advertising how Spooner's days ended in Rhone city?

indicators.note: Spooner's signals that the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: Lyon is the French city on the Rhone
nights come when days end

explanation.surface: A question about how evenings close in a French city, framed as advertising.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of LYON and NIGHTS and you hear the advertising signs.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing gas-filled tube signs are a classic medium for shop and street advertising.

clue.text: Glimpsed English and French kings splitting partition

indicators.note: splitting says the kings break into the word for glimpsed

parts.note: glimpsed means seen
K is king in English chess notation; R is roi, French for king (also Latin rex)

explanation.surface: Two royals from either side of the Channel sit behind a screen that divides a hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A skreen is an old or dialect spelling of screen, a dividing partition in a hall or church.

clue.text: Smoke out the President, 11 to 25

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of smoke are thrown into disorder

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, US President

explanation.surface: A call to drive the President out of hiding with smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the term of address the sidekick uses for his masked friend in the radio and TV western.

clue.text: See 18
See 18
18 doing good single movement between sides

indicators.note: between says the other pieces sit inside the two sides

parts.note: L and R are left and right, the two sides
single means one
range of movement is the scope a limb or machine can travel through

explanation.surface: A white man on a charitable mission moves alone from side to side.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is the cross-reference to the phrase beginning WHITE MAN; a masked hero helping the needy fits.
explanation.definitionFit: The masked hero of the western serials is a white lawman who rides about righting wrongs.

clue.text: See 18
(As 25 might) season ticket holder will regularly hide

definitions.text: (As 25 might) season ticket holder will regularly
definitions.meaning: a football fan with a season ticket regularly attends the stadium, said in the clipped pidgin of the sidekick, dropping 'the'
to hide like a fox in its earth

explanation.surface: Imitating a sidekick's speech, a fan's regular habit becomes a way of hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: Tonto's stylised speech drops articles, so 'go to the ground' becomes the idiom for going into hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to earth like a hunted fox is the idiom for hiding away from pursuers.

clue.text: Not knowing it's turning out nice in the home?

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the word for home

parts.note: a nest is a home

indicators.note: turning out suggests the letters of nice are changed round

explanation.surface: Someone unaware, finding the weather turning pleasant at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is only a link; the question mark flags that 'nice' turning out is the anagram, with 'in' placing its result inside the home.
explanation.definitionFit: Nescient is a literary adjective for ignorant, lacking knowledge.

clue.text: Make declaration about convulsions, however confined

indicators.note: about here turns the whole assembled piece round
confined says the fits sit inside the word for however

parts.note: yet means however
fits are convulsions

explanation.surface: A speaker makes a statement concerning seizures, though they are restricted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the whole container, not just the convulsions, so the letters run backwards as Y-FITS-ET turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: To testify is to make a formal statement, especially as a witness.

clue.text: One-time press cub taken in by sweet tart

indicators.note: taken in by says the novice sits inside the tart

parts.note: a flan is an open tart
a cub reporter is a tiro, a beginner

explanation.surface: A trainee journalist working on a former newspaper is fooled by a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' suggests newspapers, and 'cub' a reporter; the press is for clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatiron is the old-fashioned heavy iron heated on a stove for pressing clothes.

clue.text: Bird of prey taking my sea bird with a double heart?

parts.note: my and gosh are both exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: the middle letter of the sea bird is swapped for a double U

parts.note: the auk is a diving sea bird

explanation.surface: A hawk eats a sea bird, which is surprisingly brave.
explanation.walkthrough: W is said 'double U', so the U at the centre of AUK becomes W.
explanation.definitionFit: The goshawk is a large hawk, a raptor used in falconry.

clue.text: (As 25 might) somehow know how "pure" Enigmatist faked the accounts for this

indicators.note: somehow implies the following letters are assembled in some other fashion

explanation.surface: In a sidekick's voice, a cheating setter's fake purity is explained.
explanation.walkthrough: The full answer is the stereotyped western line WHITE MAN SPEAK WITH FORKED TONGUE, what Tonto might say to account for a deceiver; '(As 25 might)' says the line is in Tonto's voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Accusing a white man of lying is the line that would explain the setter's deceit, voiced by the sidekick.

clue.text: Setter has hot turns in bed, needing cloth

indicators.note: in puts the reversed letters within the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: turns says the setter's words and the hot letter are read backwards

parts.note: the setter says I've, I have
H is hot on a tap

explanation.surface: The compiler, tossing in a hot bed, needs some fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter has' is the compiler speaking of themself as 'I've'; 'turns' sends that and H backwards before 'in' puts them inside the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheviot is a woollen cloth from the wool of Cheviot sheep.

clue.text: What about Napoleon accepting blame for inscription?

indicators.note: about says the word for what goes round the rest

parts.note: eh? is said for what?
Napoleon is the pig leader in Orwell's Animal Farm
to take the rap is to take the blame

explanation.surface: A question about the French emperor taking the blame.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon is not the emperor here but the boar who rules Orwell's Animal Farm.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigraph is an inscription on a building or a quotation at the start of a book.

clue.text: Tip of toe indicated details — what to find at 90 degrees?

indicators.note: de-tails, read literally, means its tail is removed

parts.note: to have pointed is to have indicated

explanation.surface: A dancer's toe is described in detail, along with what is found at a right angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what to find at 90 degrees?' is an extra tease: on a compass the point at 90 degrees is East, point E.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointe is the ballet position of dancing on the tips of the toes.

clue.text: Go-between for me, so South American agents dash

parts.note: in the sol-fa scale fa comes between me and so
S is South
the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

explanation.surface: A go-between for me, so American agents rush off.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'go-between' is a note of the sol-fa scale, not a messenger.
explanation.definitionFit: A fascia is a car's dashboard, often shortened to dash.

clue.text: See 18
As 11 urged: "Why I avail horse — for getting around"

indicators.note: getting around suggests the words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A rider asks why to use a horse for travel.
explanation.walkthrough: The full answer is HI-HO SILVER AWAY, the masked rider's famous cry to his horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry with which the masked hero urged on his horse Silver.

clue.text: (As 25 might) chops x, y and z

definitions.meaning: chops, as in cuts with a hatchet, in the clipped speech of the sidekick
the three coordinate lines of a graph in three dimensions

explanation.surface: In a sidekick's voice, someone cuts three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb for cutting with a chopper, and the plural of axis, the lines of a coordinate graph.

clue.text: See 23
Leader of tribe now aware of 11's sidekick

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to be onto something is to have found it out

explanation.surface: A tribal chief realises who the hero's companion is.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonto is the Native American companion of the masked western hero.

clue.text: "Oh, for a break!" A time one collapsed at La Scala

indicators.note: break says the word for oh is split open

parts.note: per means for a, as in once per day
T is time

explanation.surface: A weary opera-goer longs for an interval at the Milan opera house.
explanation.walkthrough: La Scala is the Milan opera house; the hat is the collapsible top hat worn there.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera hat, or gibus, is a top hat that folds flat, to fit under a theatre seat.
